::: {.callout-important}
## Conclusion in one paragraph

The BLAST/LCA step assigned 10,390 contigs from 104 samples to *North shore virus*
(NSV, taxid 2485875). **Only 9 contigs, from 4 *Ixodes* samples, are genuine NSV.**
They match the RdRp at the protein level along their entire length, have intact
reading frames, and carry no tick sequence.

The other ~10,380 contigs are **tick genomic repeats**. More than 95% of them hit a
sequence that every NSV reference record carries at its 5′ end, upstream of the viral
sequence:

- 65–365 nt in the 2021 OL4521xx records;
- ~65 nt in the original 2018 record, MK026569.

That element has these properties:

- it occurs ~9,300 times across these contigs;
- it sits in highly diverse genomic contexts, on both sides;
- it co-hits tick genome annotations;
- it begins with a tRNA-like motif typical of SINE repeats;
- it is present in *Amblyomma*, *Ixodes*, *Bothriocroton* and *Cryptocroton*, but
  essentially absent from *Haemaphysalis*.

In our DNA data it is **never** joined to viral sequence. A second, smaller element at
the 3′ end of MK026569 (positions ~1650–1750) accounts for ~300 *Ixodes* contigs.

None of this is an endogenous viral element: no tick-genomic contig contains viral
coding sequence. Whether the virus's own 5′ UTR genuinely contains this SINE-like
sequence, or both independent reference assemblies are chimeras, cannot be settled
from DNA data (see *Open question*).
:::

# Background and question

This is the same question as `../Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus/are_these_real.qmd`.
NSV is an RNA virus. Our libraries come from DNA extracts (without RNase treatment), so
are these contigs:

1. genuine viral RNA carried through the extraction;
2. **endogenous viral elements (EVEs)**, i.e. viral sequence integrated into the tick
   genome and flanked by tick DNA; or
3. something else, such as a tick sequence mis-assigned through the reference database?

Lines of evidence used:

- contig length vs viral-hit length;
- where the hits fall on the reference records;
- a protein-level (tblastn) RdRp search;
- reading-frame integrity of the genuine hits;
- copy number, flank diversity and genus distribution of the shared elements;
- whether any contig joins those elements to viral sequence.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Set-up: paths, tool locations and plotting helpers"
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

ROOT <- "/data/hb-austick/work/AlexG_data/Barker_ticks/microbe_analysis/old_analysis"
NSV  <- file.path(ROOT, "extracting_pathogens/north_shore_virus")
W    <- file.path(NSV, "are_these_real")          # all intermediate files land here
dir.create(file.path(W, "ncbi"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Bash chunks inherit these. BLAST+, cd-hit and python3 come from the base
# miniforge install; seqkit is the system copy.
Sys.setenv(ROOT = ROOT, NSV = NSV, W = W, TAXID = "2485875",
           PATH = paste("/data/hb-austick/work/miniforge3/bin", "/usr/bin",
                        Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep = ":"))

col_main <- "#014B87"   # CSIRO Ocean Blue
col_alt  <- "#E87721"   # CSIRO Orange
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                plot.title.position = "plot"))
rd <- function(f, ...) read.delim(file.path(W, f), check.names = FALSE, ...)
md <- read.delim(file.path(ROOT, "metadata/sample_metadata.tsv")) |>
  mutate(tick_genus = ifelse(is.na(tick_genus) | tick_genus == "", "(unrecorded)", tick_genus))
```

# Extraction

Upstream, every SPAdes contig was searched with `blastn` (megablast) against NCBI nt
(2025-05-04 snapshot), using `-max_target_seqs 10 -evalue 1e-5`, and an LCA was computed
per contig. `extract_north_shore_virus.sh` is the Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus extraction
script with the taxid changed. It writes, per sample:

- every contig with LCA = taxid 2485875 (`fasta/`);
- **all** BLAST hits of those contigs (`blast/`);
- the LCA rows (`lca_assignments.tsv`).

::: {.callout-note}
The script had one fix. The LCA file for `8334-AMLoculosum-BriddledTurn7` carries a
trailing `7` that its contigs and BLAST files lack. The first run stopped there (under
`set -e`) after 55 of 104 samples. The script now falls back to the longest contigs
file name that is a prefix of the sample name, and logs a `NOTE`. The Cheeloo
Jingmen-like virus extraction was not affected: its 50 samples all extracted, and 8334
had no Jingmen contigs.

As before, `-max_target_seqs 10` means a **missing** tick hit is weak evidence and a
**present** one is informative.
:::

```{bash}
#| label: show-extract
#| code-summary: "The extraction script (run once, outside this document)"
cat "$NSV/extract_north_shore_virus.sh"
echo; echo "---- log notes ----"; grep -E "NOTE|WARN" "$NSV/extract.log" || echo none
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-table
#| code-summary: "Per-sample extraction summary"
summ <- read.delim(file.path(NSV, "summary.tsv")) |>
  left_join(select(md, sample_id, tick_genus, tick_species), by = c("sample" = "sample_id"))
cat(sprintf("%d samples, %s contigs, %s bp, %s BLAST hits\n", nrow(summ),
            format(sum(summ$n_contigs), big.mark = ","), format(sum(summ$total_bp), big.mark = ","),
            format(sum(summ$n_blast_hits), big.mark = ",")))
summ |> count(tick_genus, name = "samples") |> arrange(desc(samples)) |>
  kable(caption = "Samples with NSV-assigned contigs, by tick genus")
kable(arrange(summ, desc(total_bp)) |> head(15), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      caption = "15 samples with the most NSV-assigned sequence")
```

NSV is a ~1.8 kb RdRp segment, yet 104 samples from six genera carry 9.8 Mb of
"NSV" sequence, often hundreds of contigs per sample.

# Contig length vs viral-hit length

```{bash}
#| label: per-contig-coverage
#| code-summary: "Per-contig viral vs non-viral hit coverage (python)"
cd "$W"
cat "$NSV"/blast/*.tsv | grep -v '^qaccver' > allhits.tsv
python3 - <<'EOF'
import collections, re, glob, os
J = os.environ["TAXID"]
q = collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"j": set(), "o": set(), "ot": set()})
for f in glob.glob(os.environ["NSV"] + "/blast/*.tsv"):
    s = os.path.basename(f).split(".north_shore_virus")[0]
    for ln in open(f):
        if ln.startswith("qaccver"): continue
        a = ln.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        qs, qe = sorted((int(a[11]), int(a[12])))
        d = q[(s, a[0])]
        if a[6] == J: d["j"].update(range(qs, qe + 1))
        else: d["o"].update(range(qs, qe + 1)); d["ot"].add(a[4])
with open("contig_cov.tsv", "w") as o:
    o.write("sample\tcontig\tlen\tkmer_cov\tviral_bp\tviral_frac\tother_bp\tother_only_bp\tother_taxa\n")
    for (s, c), d in q.items():
        L = int(re.search(r"length_(\d+)", c).group(1))
        cov = float(re.search(r"cov_([\d.]+)", c).group(1))
        jb = len(d["j"])
        o.write("\t".join(map(str, [s, c, L, cov, jb, round(jb / L, 4), len(d["o"]),
                len(d["o"] - d["j"]), ";".join(sorted(d["ot"]))])) + "\n")
print("contigs written:", len(q))
EOF
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-len-vs-hit
#| fig-cap: "Contig length vs the length covered by North shore virus hits. The dashed line is y = x (a contig entirely covered by viral hits). Most contigs carry a short (~70 bp) hit, however long they are."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
cc <- rd("contig_cov.tsv") |>
  mutate(tick = ifelse(other_bp > 0, "Also has a non-viral (mostly tick) hit", "Viral hits only"))
ggplot(cc, aes(len, viral_bp, colour = tick)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_alt, col_main), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Contig length (bp, log)", y = "bp covered by viral hits (log)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
cat(sprintf("Viral hit span: median %d bp, max %d bp. Contig length: median %d, max %s bp. %d contigs (%.1f%%) also hit a non-viral subject.\n",
            median(cc$viral_bp), max(cc$viral_bp), median(cc$len),
            format(max(cc$len), big.mark = ","), sum(cc$other_bp > 0), 100 * mean(cc$other_bp > 0)))
```

# Where the hits fall on the reference records

## The references

```{bash}
#| label: fetch-refs
#| code-summary: "Fetch every hit reference record (plus proteins) from NCBI"
# The nt snapshot is not mounted on this machine, so the public records are
# fetched from NCBI E-utilities. Cached: only fetched if absent.
cd "$W"
awk -F'\t' -v t="$TAXID" '$7==t' allhits.tsv > jhits.tsv
cut -f2 jhits.tsv | sort -u > jrefs.ids
E="https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nuccore"
ids=$(paste -sd, jrefs.ids)
[ -s ncbi/jrefs.fa ]     || curl -s "$E&id=$ids&rettype=fasta&retmode=text" > ncbi/jrefs.fa
[ -s ncbi/jrefs.gb ]     || curl -s "$E&id=$ids&rettype=gb&retmode=text"    > ncbi/jrefs.gb
# Proteins of every hit record plus MW741889 (a third, independent NSV RdRp)
[ -s ncbi/nsv_prot.fa ]  || curl -s "$E&id=$ids,MW741889.1&rettype=fasta_cds_aa&retmode=text" > ncbi/nsv_prot.fa
seqkit grep -r -p MK026569 ncbi/jrefs.fa > mk.fa
echo "records hit: $(wc -l < jrefs.ids)"
awk '/^LOCUS/{l=$2" "$3"bp"} /^DEFINITION/{d=substr($0,13,70)} /\/host=/{h=$0; sub(/.*host=/,"",h)} /^  TITLE/{t=substr($0,13,60)} /^\/\//{print l" | "d" | "h" | "t; t=""}' ncbi/jrefs.gb | sort -u -t'|' -k1,1 | sed -n '1p;/MK026569/p;/OL452128/p'
grep -c "Gofton" ncbi/jrefs.gb | xargs echo "records submitted by Gofton,A.W.:"
cut -f2 jhits.tsv | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -8
```

There are 23 records. Twenty-two are the 2021 OL4521xx records: *I. holocyclus*,
Trinity-assembled, submitted from CSIRO. The 23rd is **MK026569**, the original 2018 NSV
segment 1 RdRp from the Sydney "Extensive diversity of RNA viruses in Australian ticks"
study. It was assembled independently and acts as the control here.

## Defining the viral core of each record

Each OL record was aligned to MK026569. They all match it at 96–99% from MK026569
position ~2 onwards, but differ in how much **extra** sequence they carry beyond it at
the 5′ end (3–300 nt) and the 3′ end. Every hit was then placed on the MK026569 coordinate
system, with 5′ overhang positions taking values ≤ 0.

```{bash}
#| label: core
#| code-summary: "Align each reference to MK026569 and map every hit onto MK026569 coordinates"
cd "$W"
blastn -task blastn -query ncbi/jrefs.fa -subject mk.fa -evalue 1e-10 \
       -outfmt '6 qseqid qlen qstart qend sstart send pident length' > core_vs_mk.tsv
python3 - <<'EOF'
import collections, glob, os
core = {}
for l in sorted(open("core_vs_mk.tsv"), key=lambda l: -int(l.split()[7])):
    a = l.split()
    if a[0] not in core: core[a[0]] = (int(a[2]), int(a[3]), int(a[4]), int(a[1]), float(a[6]))
with open("ref_core.tsv", "w") as o:
    o.write("acc\tlen\tcore_start\tcore_end\tmk_start\tpident\toverhang5\toverhang3\n")
    for k, (cs, ce, ms, L, p) in sorted(core.items()):
        o.write(f"{k}\t{L}\t{cs}\t{ce}\t{ms}\t{p}\t{cs-1}\t{L-ce}\n")
# Region boundaries in MK026569 coordinates. CDS = 180..1373 (GenBank). The
# 5' element runs into MK026569 to ~65 (shown below), so 1..65 is grouped with
# the overhang. Indels between records are ignored (all are 96-99% identical).
def region(m):
    return ("5' element" if m <= 65 else "viral 5' UTR" if m < 180 else
            "RdRp CDS" if m <= 1373 else "viral 3' UTR" if m <= 1770 else "3' overhang")
with open("hits_mk.tsv", "w") as o:
    o.write("sample\tcontig\tref\tpident\tlength\tmk_start\tmk_end\tregion\n")
    for f in glob.glob(os.environ["NSV"] + "/blast/*.tsv"):
        s = os.path.basename(f).split(".north_shore_virus")[0]
        for l in open(f):
            if l.startswith("qaccver"): continue
            a = l.split("\t")
            if a[6] != os.environ["TAXID"]: continue
            st, e = sorted((int(a[13]), int(a[14])))
            cs, ce, ms, L, p = core[a[1]]
            m1, m2 = st - cs + ms, e - cs + ms
            o.write(f"{s}\t{a[0]}\t{a[1]}\t{a[7]}\t{a[8]}\t{m1}\t{m2}\t{region((m1+m2)/2)}\n")
EOF
column -t ref_core.tsv
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-depth
#| fig-cap: "Hit depth along the North shore virus segment, in MK026569 coordinates (positions ≤ 0 are 5′ overhang present only in the OL records; > 1,770 is 3′ overhang). Shaded: the RdRp CDS. Almost all hits pile up on the 5′ element; a smaller peak sits at the 3′ end of MK026569; the CDS is barely touched."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
hm <- rd("hits_mk.tsv")
depth <- hm |> rowwise() |> reframe(pos = seq(mk_start, mk_end)) |> count(pos, name = "hits")
# positions with no hit must be explicit zeros, or geom_area bridges the gaps
depth <- complete(depth, pos = full_seq(pos, 1), fill = list(hits = 0L))
ggplot(depth, aes(pos, hits)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 180, xmax = 1373, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, fill = col_main, alpha = 0.08) +
  annotate("text", x = 776, y = max(depth$hits) * 0.9, label = "RdRp CDS", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.5, 1770.5), linetype = 3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_area(fill = col_main, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_y_sqrt(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Position (MK026569 coordinates)", y = "BLAST hits covering position (sqrt)")
```

```{r}
#| label: region-table
#| code-summary: "Hits and contigs per region; one region per contig by priority"
lev <- c("RdRp CDS", "viral 5' UTR", "viral 3' UTR", "3' overhang", "5' element")
hm |> group_by(region) |>
  summarise(hits = n(), contigs = n_distinct(paste(sample, contig)), samples = n_distinct(sample),
            median_hit_len = median(length)) |>
  arrange(match(region, lev)) |> kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
                                     caption = "Every hit, by region of the NSV segment it lands on")
# one class per contig: CDS wins (a contig with any CDS hit is a candidate virus),
# otherwise the region with most hits
contig_class <- hm |> count(sample, contig, region) |>
  group_by(sample, contig) |>
  summarise(class = if (any(region == "RdRp CDS")) "RdRp CDS" else region[which.max(n)], .groups = "drop")
contig_class |> left_join(select(md, sample_id, tick_genus), by = c("sample" = "sample_id")) |>
  count(class, tick_genus) |> pivot_wider(names_from = tick_genus, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(match(class, lev)) |> kable(caption = "Contigs per class, by tick genus")
```

# Which contigs are actually viral?

## Protein-level search

This uses the RdRp proteins of all 23 hit records plus MW741889 (a third, independent NSV
RdRp), searched with tblastn against all 10,390 contigs.

```{bash}
#| label: tblastn
#| code-summary: "tblastn of NSV RdRp proteins against every assigned contig"
cd "$W"
if [ ! -s nsvdb.nsq ]; then
  for f in "$NSV"/fasta/*.fasta; do
    s=$(basename "$f" .north_shore_virus.fasta)
    seqkit replace -p '^' -r "${s}|" "$f" 2>/dev/null     # prefix sample name to contig id
  done > all_nsv.fa
  makeblastdb -in all_nsv.fa -dbtype nucl -out nsvdb > /dev/null
fi
seqkit stats -T all_nsv.fa
OF='6 qseqid sseqid pident length qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore'
tblastn -query ncbi/nsv_prot.fa -db nsvdb -evalue 1e-3 -seg no -outfmt "$OF" -num_threads 2 > tbn_strict.tsv
echo "contigs with an RdRp hit at e <= 1e-3:"; cut -f2 tbn_strict.tsv | sort -u
```

The same 9 contigs are found by both routes: the nucleotide hits inside the CDS and the
protein search. Nothing else in the 10,390 contigs encodes NSV protein.

## The nine genuine contigs

```{bash}
#| label: genuine
#| code-summary: "Coverage of MK026569, reading frames and non-viral hits for the 9 contigs"
cd "$W"
cut -f2 tbn_strict.tsv | sort -u > cds.ids
seqkit grep -f cds.ids all_nsv.fa > cds_contigs.fa 2>/dev/null
echo "== alignment to MK026569 (best HSP per contig) =="
blastn -task blastn -query cds_contigs.fa -subject mk.fa -evalue 1e-5 \
       -outfmt '6 qseqid qlen pident length qstart qend sstart send' |
  sort -k1,1 -k4,4nr | awk '!s[$1]++' | column -t
echo; echo "== tblastn vs MK026569 RdRp: stop codons in the aligned translation =="
seqkit grep -r -p MK026569 ncbi/nsv_prot.fa > mk_prot.fa 2>/dev/null
tblastn -query mk_prot.fa -subject cds_contigs.fa -evalue 1e-3 -seg no \
        -outfmt '6 sseqid pident length qstart qend sframe sseq' |
  sort -k1,1 -k3,3nr | awk -F'\t' '!s[$1]++{n=gsub(/\*/,"*",$7); print $1"\t"$2"%\t"$3"aa\tRdRp "$4"-"$5"\tframe "$6"\tstops "n}' | column -t
echo; echo "== non-viral BLAST hits on these contigs =="
grep -F -f <(sed 's/.*|//' cds.ids) allhits.tsv | awk -F'\t' -v t="$TAXID" '$7!=t' | wc -l
```

```{r}
#| label: genuine-meta
#| code-summary: "Samples carrying genuine NSV"
data.frame(id = readLines(file.path(W, "cds.ids"))) |>
  mutate(sample = sub("\\|.*", "", id)) |> count(sample, name = "contigs") |>
  left_join(select(md, sample_id, tick_species, life_stage, host_species, collection_site),
            by = c("sample" = "sample_id")) |> kable()
```

All 9 contigs share these features:

- **Viral from end to end.** The whole contig aligns to MK026569, and there are no
  non-viral hits.
- **Low coverage.** k-mer coverage is 0.1–2.2×, as expected for RNA carried over into a
  DNA extract.
- ***Ixodes* only.** They come from four samples: two *I. holocyclus* (8143 and 8337,
  the known NSV host), one *I. hirsti* and one *I. trichosuri*.
- **Strain-level divergence.** The *I. holocyclus* contigs are 97–99.6% identical to
  MK026569. The *I. hirsti* and *I. trichosuri* contigs are 91–93% (85–90% amino acid),
  consistent with distinct strains or a related virus.
- **Near-complete segment in 8337.** Its five contigs tile MK026569 positions ~26–1449.
- **Intact reading frames.** The one exception is a single stop codon in a low-coverage
  (0.47×) *I. trichosuri* contig, more likely a sequencing or assembly error than
  pseudogenisation.

Because these contigs carry no tick flanks, there is no junction. The simplest reading is
genuine viral RNA. A complete, flank-less EVE cannot be strictly excluded from these data
alone. The intact reading frames and the strain-level variation across three tick species
argue against it.

# The 5′ element: a tick repeat at the front of every reference

## Every reference carries the same element

```{bash}
#| label: overhangs
#| code-summary: "Extract each reference's 5'/3' overhang and compare them"
cd "$W"
python3 - <<'EOF' > overhangs.fa
seq, n = {}, None
for l in open("ncbi/jrefs.fa"):
    l = l.strip()
    if l.startswith(">"): n = l[1:].split()[0]; seq[n] = ""
    else: seq[n] += l
for l in list(open("ref_core.tsv"))[1:]:
    acc, L, cs, ce = l.split("\t")[:4]; L, cs, ce = int(L), int(cs), int(ce)
    if cs > 30:     print(f">{acc}_5ov_1-{cs-1}\n{seq[acc][:cs-1]}")
    if L - ce > 30: print(f">{acc}_3ov_{ce+1}-{L}\n{seq[acc][ce:]}")
EOF
# probe = the longest 5' overhang (OL452120.1, 1-299)
seqkit grep -r -p "OL452120.1_5ov" overhangs.fa > elem5.fa 2>/dev/null
echo "5' overhangs: $(grep -c '_5ov' overhangs.fa); 3' overhangs: $(grep -c '_3ov' overhangs.fa)"
echo "== each 5' overhang vs the OL452120 probe =="
blastn -task blastn -query elem5.fa -subject overhangs.fa -evalue 1e-5 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid pident length' | grep _5ov | sort -u -k1,1 | column -t
echo; echo "== first 120 nt of MK026569 (the 2018 record) =="
seqkit subseq -r 1:120 mk.fa 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d '\n'; echo
```

All 17 records with a 5′ overhang carry the same element (85–100% identical). It always
ends at the same place: immediately before MK026569 position ~2. MK026569 itself begins
`GCCGGTGTCGGGAATCGAACCTGGG…`. Its `GGGAATCGAACC` is the reverse complement of the tRNA
T-arm "B-box" (`GGTTCGAWTCC`), the hallmark of tRNA-derived SINE retrotransposons.

## Copies, flanks and junctions in our contigs

```{bash}
#| label: element
#| code-summary: "Map the 5' element onto all contigs; test for any element-virus junction"
cd "$W"
blastn -task blastn -query elem5.fa -db nsvdb -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 100000 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid slen sstart send qstart qend pident length' > elem5_hits.tsv
echo "element copies: $(wc -l < elem5_hits.tsv) on $(cut -f1 elem5_hits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l) contigs"
awk '{s=($3<$4)?$3:$4; e=($3<$4)?$4:$3; if(s<=20||e>=$2-20) a++; else b++} END{print "copies touching a contig end:",a," interior:",b}' elem5_hits.tsv

# Where does tick-genome homology stop inside MK026569? Probe its first 600 nt.
seqkit subseq -r 1:600 mk.fa 2>/dev/null > mk_head.fa
blastn -task blastn -query mk_head.fa -db nsvdb -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 100000 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid sstart send qstart qend pident' > mk_head_hits.tsv
cut -f1 elem5_hits.tsv | sort -u > e5.ids
grep -v -F -f cds.ids mk_head_hits.tsv | cut -f1 | sort -u > mkhead_nongenuine.ids
echo "non-genuine contigs hitting MK026569 1-600: $(wc -l < mkhead_nongenuine.ids); of which also carry the element: $(comm -12 e5.ids mkhead_nongenuine.ids | wc -l)"
echo "furthest MK026569 position reached by those contigs: $(grep -v -F -f cds.ids mk_head_hits.tsv | awk '{if($5>m)m=$5}END{print m}')"
echo "distribution of that end point (10-nt bins):"
grep -v -F -f cds.ids mk_head_hits.tsv | awk '{print int($5/10)*10}' | sort -n | uniq -c | awk '{printf "  MK %s: %s\n",$2,$1}'
```

```{bash}
#| label: e5-flanks
#| code-summary: "Flank diversity on both sides of the element (cd-hit-est, 90%)"
cd "$W"
python3 - <<'EOF'
seqs, name = {}, None
for l in open("all_nsv.fa"):
    l = l.strip()
    if l.startswith(">"): name = l[1:].split()[0]; seqs[name] = []
    else: seqs[name].append(l)
seqs = {k: "".join(v) for k, v in seqs.items()}
comp = str.maketrans("ACGTNacgtn", "TGCANtgcan")
# "up" = 150 bp before the element (away from the virus in the references);
# "down" = 150 bp after the element's 3' end, i.e. where the VIRUS sits in the
# references. Only copies that reach the probe's 3' end (>=290/299) count as "down".
for side in ("up", "down"):
    seen = set(); o = open(f"e5_{side}.fa", "w")
    for l in open("elem5_hits.tsv"):
        c, slen, ss, se, qs, qe = l.split("\t")[:6]
        ss, se, slen, qe = int(ss), int(se), int(slen), int(qe)
        if c in seen: continue
        plus = ss < se
        if side == "up":
            if plus and ss > 150: f = seqs[c][ss - 151:ss - 1]
            elif not plus and ss + 150 <= slen: f = seqs[c][ss:ss + 150][::-1].translate(comp)
            else: continue
        else:
            if qe < 290: continue
            if plus and se + 150 <= slen: f = seqs[c][se:se + 150]
            elif not plus and se > 150: f = seqs[c][se - 151:se - 1][::-1].translate(comp)
            else: continue
        seen.add(c); o.write(f">{c}\n{f}\n")
    print(f"{side}: {len(seen)} flanks")
EOF
for s in up down; do
  cd-hit-est -i e5_$s.fa -o e5_${s}_c90 -c 0.9 -n 8 -T 2 -M 3000 -d 0 > /dev/null
  echo "$s: $(grep -c '^>Cluster' e5_${s}_c90.clstr) clusters; largest: $(awk '/^>Cluster/{if(n)print n; n=0; next}{n++} END{print n}' e5_${s}_c90.clstr | sort -rn | head -4 | paste -sd' ')"
done
```

The results:

- **Copy number.** The element occurs ~9,300 times, on ~9,200 contigs.
- **Viral side of the element.** In the references, the virus follows the element. In
  our contigs, the 150 bp after the element are essentially **all different**: about
  860 flanks form about 830 clusters.
- **The other side.** The 150 bp before the element are also diverse: about 3,560
  flanks form about 2,200 clusters.
- **Where the homology stops.** In about 1,100 contigs, the tick-genome homology
  continues into MK026569 but stops at position ~60–70 (never beyond ~100). So the
  first ~65 nt of the 2018 record are the element too.
- **No junction.** No contig joins the element on to NSV coding sequence.

This is the signature of an interspersed repeat, such as a SINE, at many sites in the
tick genome. It is not an integrated virus.

## Genus distribution

```{r}
#| label: fig-genus
#| fig-cap: "Copies of the 5′ element, by tick genus. Labels: samples with the element / samples sequenced."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
e5 <- read.delim(file.path(W, "elem5_hits.tsv"), header = FALSE)
copies <- e5 |> mutate(sample_id = sub("\\|.*", "", V1)) |> count(sample_id, name = "copies")
gtab <- md |> select(sample_id, tick_genus) |> left_join(copies, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(copies = coalesce(copies, 0L)) |> group_by(tick_genus) |>
  summarise(samples = n(), with_element = sum(copies > 0), copies = sum(copies)) |>
  arrange(desc(copies))
kable(gtab, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
ggplot(gtab, aes(reorder(tick_genus, copies), copies)) +
  geom_col(fill = col_main, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d/%d", with_element, samples)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "5′ element copies across all samples")
```

```{r}
#| label: e5-cohits
#| code-summary: "Non-viral subjects on element-bearing contigs"
e5c <- unique(e5$V1)
ah <- read.delim(file.path(W, "allhits.tsv"), header = FALSE, quote = "")
names(ah) <- strsplit("qaccver saccver stitle sseqid ssciname scomname staxid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore", " ")[[1]]
cc_e5 <- cc |> filter(paste0(sample, "|", contig) %in% e5c)
nv <- ah |> filter(staxid != 2485875, qaccver %in% cc_e5$contig)
nv |> distinct(qaccver, ssciname) |> count(ssciname, sort = TRUE, name = "n_contigs") |> head(10) |>
  kable(caption = "Non-viral taxa on element-bearing contigs (contig IDs are per-sample, so counts are approximate)")
```

The element is spread across *Amblyomma*, *Ixodes*, *Bothriocroton* and *Cryptocroton*.
Its co-hits are predicted genes from metastriate tick genomes (*Dermacentor*,
*Rhipicephalus*), some annotated as transposon-derived. It is essentially absent from
all 34 *Haemaphysalis* samples, which is unexpected given how closely *Haemaphysalis* is
related to *Amblyomma*. It could reflect lineage-specific loss or expansion of a SINE
family, and is worth following up.

This is **not** the same element as the Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus one:

```{bash}
#| label: vs-cjv
#| code-summary: "Compare with the Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus element"
cd "$W"
blastn -task blastn -query elem5.fa -subject "$ROOT/extracting_pathogens/Cheeloo_Jingmen-like_virus/are_these_real/elem.fa" \
       -evalue 10 -outfmt '6 pident length qstart qend sstart send evalue' | head -3
echo "(no output above = no similarity at e <= 10)"
```

# The 3′ end of MK026569: a second, smaller element

About 300 contigs hit the last ~120 nt of MK026569 (positions ~1650–1770), beyond the
CDS. A further ~400 hit the 3′ overhangs of the OL records.

```{bash}
#| label: e3
#| code-summary: "Probe MK026569 1374-1770 (3' UTR) against all contigs"
cd "$W"
seqkit subseq -r 1374:1770 mk.fa 2>/dev/null > mk3.fa
blastn -task blastn -query mk3.fa -db nsvdb -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 100000 \
       -outfmt '6 sseqid slen sstart send qstart qend pident length' | grep -v -F -f cds.ids > mk3_hits.tsv
echo "copies: $(wc -l < mk3_hits.tsv) on $(cut -f1 mk3_hits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l) contigs (genuine contigs excluded)"
echo "hit start in MK026569 coordinates (50-nt bins):"
awk '{print int(($5+1373)/50)*50}' mk3_hits.tsv | sort -n | uniq -c | awk '{printf "  MK %s: %s\n",$2,$1}'
awk '{print $2}' mk3_hits.tsv | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{print "contig length: median",a[int(NR/2)],"max",a[NR]}'
awk '{print $8}' mk3_hits.tsv | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=$1} END{print "hit length: median",a[int(NR/2)]}'
echo "genus:"; cut -f1 mk3_hits.tsv | sed 's/|.*//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn |
  awk 'NR==FNR{g[$1]=$5; next} {c[g[$2]]+=$1} END{for(k in c) print "  "k": "c[k]}' FS='\t' "$ROOT/metadata/sample_metadata.tsv" FS=' ' -
```

```{r}
#| label: e3-cohits
#| code-summary: "Non-viral subjects on 3'-element contigs"
e3 <- read.delim(file.path(W, "mk3_hits.tsv"), header = FALSE)
ah |> filter(staxid != 2485875, qaccver %in% sub(".*\\|", "", unique(e3$V1))) |>
  distinct(qaccver, ssciname) |> count(ssciname, sort = TRUE, name = "n_contigs") |> head(8) |>
  kable(caption = "Non-viral taxa on 3'-element contigs")
```

These are again short hits (median ~80 bp) inside longer contigs (median ~600 bp, up
to 16.7 kb), restricted to *Ixodes*. Few contigs have non-viral co-hits, and those that
do mostly hit tick genomes (*I. scapularis*, *Dermacentor*, *Rhipicephalus*). The 3′ end
of MK026569 therefore also appears to carry ~100 nt of *Ixodes* repeat. This element is
minor, and its flank diversity was not tested. It is less certain than the 5′ element:
it could still be a genuine viral 3′ UTR with homology to an *Ixodes* repeat.

# Open question: is the 5′ element part of the virus?

Two independent assemblies begin with the same element: MK026569 (2018) and the 22 OL
records (2021). Each of the 17 OL overhangs ends at exactly the same point. There are
two readings:

(a) **Assembly chimera (favoured).** A highly expressed tick SINE transcript shares a
    short sequence with the NSV 5′ terminus, and Trinity bridges them. The same artefact
    would then recur in every assembly from *I. holocyclus* RNA-seq, at the same
    junction. The overhang lengths vary widely (3–300 nt) while the junction stays
    fixed, which fits this.

(b) **The virus genuinely carries the sequence.** NSV's 5′ UTR may itself contain a
    SINE-like or tRNA-like sequence, captured from the host. That would make the tick
    copies host repeats that are merely *related* to the viral UTR, not virus-derived
    insertions.

Neither reading changes the conclusion for our data. The 9,800 element-bearing contigs
are tick genomic repeats, not NSV and not EVEs. The question can be settled with:

- **Original read data.** Map the RNA-seq reads behind MK026569 and the OL records onto
  them. A chimera shows a coverage step at the junction, and few or no read pairs span
  it. A genuine UTR shows continuous coverage.
- **5′ RACE** on NSV-positive *I. holocyclus* RNA, to define the true viral 5′ terminus.
- **Repeat classification.** Search the element against an *I. holocyclus* or
  *I. scapularis* genome assembly and Dfam, or run RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker, to name
  the SINE family.

# Conclusions

1. **Genuine NSV is rare: 9 contigs in 4 *Ixodes* samples.** These are *I. holocyclus*
   8143 and 8337, *I. hirsti* B5119 and *I. trichosuri* B6836. The contigs are viral
   from end to end, have intact RdRp frames and are low-coverage, consistent with
   co-extracted viral RNA. The *I. hirsti* and *I. trichosuri* sequences are divergent
   (91–93% nt) and may be distinct strains.
2. **The other ~10,380 "NSV" contigs are tick genomic repeats.** About 95% of them carry
   a SINE-like element that sits at the 5′ end of every NSV reference record. A few
   hundred *Ixodes* contigs carry a second element from the 3′ end of MK026569.
3. **No evidence of NSV EVEs.** No tick-genomic contig contains viral coding sequence,
   and no contig joins either element to the virus.
4. **The reference records, not our data, hold the virus–repeat junction.** This is the
   same kind of reference artefact as Cheeloo Jingmen-like virus, but with a different
   element and a different genus range.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Implications for the pipeline and reporting

- Report NSV only for 8143, 8337-Iholo-Xbtp-Awzh, B5119_F1_S15 and B6836_N1_S13 (or,
  more generally, contigs with RdRp protein support).
- Before LCA, mask the 5′ overhangs and MK026569 positions 1–~100 and 1650–1770 (or the
  whole UTRs) in the NSV references. Otherwise, require protein-level support for any
  viral call.
- Several of these references are our own (Gofton, CSIRO, 2021). Consider submitting
  trimmed versions, or adding a note to the records.
:::

# Files and versions

All intermediate files are in `are_these_real/` beside this document. The extraction
outputs (`fasta/`, `blast/`, `ids/`, `summary.tsv`, `lca_assignments.tsv`, `extract.log`)
are in this directory.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `allhits.tsv`, `jhits.tsv` | all BLAST hits for the assigned contigs; NSV subset |
| `contig_cov.tsv` | per-contig viral vs non-viral hit coverage |
| `ncbi/` | reference records and proteins fetched from NCBI |
| `core_vs_mk.tsv`, `ref_core.tsv` | each reference aligned to MK026569; its core and overhangs |
| `hits_mk.tsv` | every NSV hit in MK026569 coordinates, with region |
| `all_nsv.fa`, `nsvdb.*` | all assigned contigs (sample-prefixed) and BLAST db |
| `tbn_strict.tsv`, `cds.ids`, `cds_contigs.fa` | tblastn results; the 9 genuine contigs |
| `overhangs.fa`, `elem5.fa`, `elem5_hits.tsv` | reference overhangs; 5′ element probe and its copies |
| `mk_head_hits.tsv` | hits of MK026569 1–600 (junction test) |
| `e5_up*`, `e5_down*` | element flanks and cd-hit-est clusters |
| `mk3.fa`, `mk3_hits.tsv` | MK026569 3′ UTR probe and its copies |
